references.text: The preceding context where Israel made a vow to the Lord to devote the Canaanite cities to destruction if He gave them victory.
Judah and Simeon struck down the Canaanites living in Zephath and devoted the city to destruction, so it was called Hormah.
Hormah is mentioned in connection with Israel's defeat when they tried to enter the land without the Lord's blessing.
Parallel account of Israel's defeat at Hormah in Moses' retelling.
The king of Hormah is listed among the kings whom Joshua defeated.
Hormah is recorded as one of the cities in Judah's inheritance.
Hormah is mentioned as one of the cities in Simeon's inheritance.
David sent spoils of war to those living in Hormah.
The law of herem (ban) where cities and people were devoted to complete destruction.
Jericho was devoted to destruction (herem) as an example of how the ban law was practiced.
